findings.title: Choose instant-based temporal equivalence, accepting two measured compatibility changes
findings.detail: Recommendation: use a true equivalence relation based on temporal meaning, not Python's non-transitive/hash-sensitive edge cases. The proposed classes are: aware datetime/Timestamp values are equal iff they denote the same UTC instant, independent of UTC/IANA/pytz/fixed-offset provider; naive datetime/Timestamp/np.datetime64 values are equal iff their exact wall-time coordinate is equal; aware and naive remain distinct; datetime.date remains distinct from midnight datetime/Timestamp; fixed durations (pd.Timedelta, datetime.timedelta, and fixed-unit np.timedelta64) are equal by exact duration; np.timedelta64 Y/M use a separate calendar-month class, with 1Y equal to 12M but incomparable to days; tuples and frozensets recurse through these rules. This keeps today's collapse of UTC versus New York, ordinary fixed-offset versus zoneinfo, ordinary pytz versus zoneinfo, datetime versus Timestamp, Timestamp s versus ns, equal np.datetime64 units and np.datetime64 versus Timestamp, equal np.timedelta64 units, pd.Timedelta versus datetime.timedelta, and nested equivalents. It keeps zoneinfo fold=0 versus fold=1 separate because they are two instants, keeps naive versus aware separate, and keeps date versus midnight datetime separate. It newly collapses pytz-standard versus zoneinfo-fold=1 and ambiguous fixed-offset versus zoneinfo-fold=1 at the same instant. It also deliberately separates stdlib zoneinfo datetime fold=0/fold=1, which Python currently collapses despite their being different instants. Alternatives requiring an owner decision are: (A) recommended instant identity, consistent and persistence-stable but with those compatibility changes; (B) include timezone provider/name or fold, which preserves ambiguous pairs but splits ordinary same-instant pairs that work today; or (C) mirror Python/pandas equality and hashing, which is not an equivalence relation usable as a stable key. Executed evidence on pandas 2.3.3/NumPy 2.2.6 and pandas 3.0.1/NumPy 2.4.2: pair+x casts produced codes [0,0,1] for UTC/NY, ordinary fixed/zoneinfo, datetime/Timestamp, Timestamp units, datetime64 units/Timestamp, timedelta forms, tuple, and frozenset; [0,1,2] for naive/aware, date/Timestamp, and zoneinfo folds. On pandas 2, pytz-standard == zoneinfo-fold=1 was True but hashes differed and pandas retained both categories. For collapsed keys, a faithful pandas cast keeps pandas' existing representative/order; a rebuilt column uses the first row representative per key. Thus its in-memory type, unit, and timezone survive. The key itself keeps only aware/naive plus the instant, so persistence may change a pytz representative to fixed offset without changing identity; zoneinfo representatives retain their IANA name through the existing codec.

findings.title: Extend the faithful-key mechanism and version the identity contract, not the artifact envelope
findings.detail: Recommended mechanism: extend category_identity_key with tagged keys such as ('temporal','date',ordinal), ('temporal','datetime','naive'|'aware',attoseconds_from_epoch), ('temporal','duration','fixed',attoseconds), and ('temporal','duration','calendar_months',months). Normalize np.datetime64 Y/M through their proleptic-Gregorian calendar start and all fixed units exactly, including ps/fs/as; use Python integers to avoid ns-range overflow. Container keys recurse. Remove holds_temporal from identity_eligible's exclusion so every all-V temporal column executes the existing cast_is_faithful predicate. A faithful all-Timestamp cast, including pandas 2's datetime64[ns,tz] categories for #379, keeps pandas' categories/mode/representative and only changes transform lookup to the key. A faithful all-datetime64 cast to Timestamp categories is likewise retained. A cast that raises or loses identity is rebuilt by key and marked as a stand-in, as H-0138 already does. This is necessary for the SAMPLES datetime folds, sub-ns datetime64 values, mixed-unit timedelta64, and the batch-dependent pandas-2 Timestamp column. The existing codec at lizyml/core/category_values.py:208 writes pytz as fixed offset; an aware-instant key is stable across that conversion and across joblib's fold reconstruction. Runtime, H-0136 comparison, generated train.py/predict.py, declared-category restoration, mode counting, and unseen lookup all need the same key. lizyml/codegen/identity_template.py:24 must carry the temporal normalization and read both identity versions. category_identity_version must become 2: version 1 explicitly meant a key that rejected temporals, and reusing 1 would let an H-0138 loader accept a temporal identity column and then fail or mis-handle it. New loaders should accept 1 and 2; unmarked and version-1 states retain their saved lookup and are never upgraded. FORMAT_VERSION can remain 5 because the state shape is unchanged and an H-0138 format-5 loader already rejects an unknown identity marker during load; bumping to 6 would only duplicate that compatibility gate. Full serialized bytes cannot literally remain identical because the marker/list changes; the meaningful bit-identical guarantee should be categories, order, representative, mode, booster inputs, and predictions for faithful columns.

findings.title: Approve the measured firing rate, including currently working datetime models that will change
findings.detail: Using an executed candidate exact-key/faithful-cast harness over the eight SAMPLES columns containing a temporal value, with the acceptance-style seeded 800-row frame: on pandas 2.3.3, 4/8 have some outcome change and 4/8 retain identical encoded categories/mode and behavior. Of the six columns that fit today, 2/6 change: datetime goes from 5 to 6 categories because its two zoneinfo folds are separated, and datetime64 goes from 12 to 15 because exact sub-ns values are retained; both change codes and mode. Exact-key surrogate fits changed predictions on 800/800 rows for each, with maximum absolute differences 0.00037265 and 0.00045505. The pandas-2 Timestamp column currently fails with 'Categorical categories must be unique' and becomes an 8-category saveable model; timedelta64 currently fails with 'from_unit must be <= to_unit' and becomes a 14-category saveable model. On pandas 3.0.1, 3/8 have some outcome change and 5/8 stay identical: the same 2/7 currently fitting datetime/datetime64 models change (max differences 0.00037265 and 0.00060625), while timedelta64 changes from a ValueError about unit Y to a 14-category saveable model. Thus the per-dimension count in both versions is 2/8 with changed existing category count/codes/mode/predictions, plus 2/8 pandas-2 or 1/8 pandas-3 changing from no fit/export outcome to successful fit/export. These are semantic corrections, but the owner must explicitly accept that they change models which run today.

findings.title: The probe population is mostly faithful, but three pandas-2 export outcomes change
findings.detail: Executed the 800-row/8-round probe from this workspace (lizyml.__file__ printed the reviewed workspace). On pandas 3.0.1, 0/15 probe columns change category count, codes, mode, predictions, or export eligibility under the recommended key; 15/15 retain the pandas categorical artifacts and prediction behavior. On pandas 2.3.3, 1/19 changes category count, codes, mode, and prediction: pytz-standard plus zoneinfo-fold=1 plus 'y' rebuilds from 3 to 2 categories, combines 510/800 rows, changes the mode from 'y' to the first temporal representative, and an exact-key surrogate changed 510/800 probabilities (max 0.00048939). The other 18/19 retain pandas' categories/order/representatives/mode and final prediction values. Export eligibility changes for 3/19: #379, pytz-standard+str, and pytz-standard+zoneinfo-fold=1 go from refused to accepted. #379 additionally stops reporting 426 unseen rows, although under this probe's mode policy its probability vector was already identical to the exact-key surrogate. Therefore 16/19 keep every listed observable including export outcome, while 18/19 keep the categorical/model artifacts apart from the required identity marker. This is the measured compatibility cost of the recommended contract.

findings.title: All in-scope H-0136 temporal refusals become saveable, including the pytz control
findings.detail: H-0136 is invoked by Model.fit warning at lizyml/core/model.py:386 and by all three exits through lizyml/persistence/exporter.py:222. Under identity version 2, its state comparison must compare keyed codes and mode codes. The ten parametrized refused temporal shapes in tests/test_persistence/test_h0136_acceptance.py become saveable when newly fitted: zoneinfo-fold=1+pytz-standard; both pytz folds; one pytz-standard under mode/nan/error; pytz-standard inside tuple/frozenset; both uint64/timedelta64-month orders; and the declared-category variant. Values outside V and old unmarked/version-1 states remain on the old rule and remain refused where they are refused today. The accepted ambiguous zoneinfo-fold=1+fixed-offset control changes from two categories to one under instant identity; the accepted 1+timedelta64(1s) control stays two because number and duration keys are disjoint. Executed preflight evidence on pandas 2.3.3 confirmed all three probe refusals. For pytz-standard+str specifically, the fitted category is pytz fold=0 with hash -2935999281878169449; joblib restores the same wall value as pytz fold=1 with hash 8034518732344066542, so pandas lookup calls the learned value unseen and export refuses. JSON instead restores fixed UTC-05:00 fold=0 with the original hash. The recommended aware-instant key is identical across all three forms, so the model becomes saveable without changing its categories, mode, codes, or predictions.

findings.title: The checked-in matrix is confirmed for executable stages, and both earlier critique claims still hold
findings.detail: Fact-check evidence: rerunning the exact probe on this head reproduced every fit warning, learned category, in-memory unseen result, and batch result in temporal_matrix_pd2.out and temporal_matrix_pd3.out. The sandbox has no writable temporary directory, so the probe's tempfile-based export/load and export_code stages returned FileNotFoundError rather than rerunning those filesystem writes; direct in-memory check_category_values execution independently reproduced the three pandas-2 SERIALIZATION_FAILED decisions and their serializer/kind. The earlier 'np.datetime64 maps six training values to the mode on pandas 3' claim is confirmed at this head, not refuted: preserving X before fit, prediction reported 338/800 rows spanning six distinct values (4ns, 4ps, 4fs, 4as, 8s via 2s ticks, and 30ms via 10ms ticks) replaced by Timestamp('1970-01-01 00:00:00'). The earlier mixed-unit np.timedelta64 claim is also confirmed: the SAMPLES cast/fit raises ValueError on both versions ('from_unit must be <= to_unit' on pandas 2.3.3; unsupported unit Y on pandas 3.0.1).
